provenance.note: Home-based program: street address, phone and provider name are not shown.

inspection_summary.note: Texas HHSC inspections, report investigations and assessments since October 2017, updated daily.

occurrences.finding: Personnel Records for Household Members - Orientation: One household member did not have record of receiving orientation.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Personnel Records for Household Members - Orientation (26 TAC §747.905(2))

occurrences.finding: Smoke-Detection System: The living room is used by children in care but did not have a smoke detector.

Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Separate from Food and Inaccessible: A bottle of Febreze was left within the reach of children. This was corrected during the inspection when the Febreze was moved out of the reach of children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Separate from Food and Inaccessible (26 TAC §747.3203(13))

occurrences.finding: Fire Drill Monthly - Exit in 3 Minutes: A fire drill had not been conducted for December. This was corrected during the inspection when a fire drill was completed and the children were able to exit within three minutes.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Fire Drill Monthly - Exit in 3 Minutes (26 TAC §747.5005(1))

occurrences.finding: Smoke Detectors Testing: The smoke detector, carbon monoxide detector, and fire extinguisher had not been checked in December. This was corrected during the inspection when the detectors and fire extinguisher were checked.

Training Requirements for Primary Caregiver -30 Hours Annual Training: The primary caregiver was missing 10 hours of annual training, including training in handling hazardous materials and injury prevention. The primary caregiver also had not received six hours of instructor-led training.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Training Requirements for Primary Caregiver -30 Hours Annual Training (26 TAC §747.1303(5)(A))

occurrences.finding: Policies Comply with Rules: The parent handbook was missing information about a new dog in the home, recommended clothing for outside time and how long children play outside, and instructions for how parents can find minimum standards online.

Children's Records - Admission Information: Out of the three children's files reviewed, three were missing dates of admission, one's emergency medical authorization was not complete, two did not have confirmation that a parent had received the operational policies, and two were missing healthcare statements

Policies Comply with Rules: The operational policies were missing a promotion of physical activity as well as the contact information for the local licensing office, the DFPS website, and the abuse/neglect hotline number.

Posting Requirements-Inspection Report: The operation did not have their most recent inspection report posted. This was corrected during the inspection when the primary caregiver printed the inspection report and posted it on the wall.
Written Activity Plan - Outdoor Play Opportunities: The daily activity plan only had one opportunity of outdoor play scheduled.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Activity Plan - Outdoor Play Opportunities (26 TAC §747.2104(a)(1))

occurrences.finding: Parent Provided Meals/Snacks - Statement on Enrollment Agreement: The operation uses meals and snacks provided by the parents, but did not have a signed statement from each parent acknowledging that they choose to provide their own food and that the child-care home is not responsible for the nutritional value of the food or meeting the children's daily food needs.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Parent Provided Meals/Snacks - Statement on Enrollment Agreement (26 TAC §747.3109(a))

occurrences.finding: Fire Drill Monthly - Exit in 3 Minutes: During the inspection there was no documentation  of fire drills being condcuted within the past eight  months. This was corrected by a fire drill being  completed.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Fire Drill Monthly - Exit in 3 Minutes (26 TAC §747.5005(1))

occurrences.finding: Written Operational Policies - Duration of Physical Activity: During the inspection the operation did not have a   policiy on the promotion of outdoor play.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Operational Policies - Duration of Physical Activity (26 TAC §747.501(8)(A))

occurrences.finding: Screen Time Activities - Not Exceed One Hour Daily: During the inspection a three year old was  observed watching a cartoon on a computer tablet  for more than the one hour per day allowance. This  was corrected during the inspection by the  caregvier removing the tablet.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Screen Time Activities - Not Exceed One Hour Daily (26 TAC §747.2105(c)(3))

occurrences.finding: Records Maintained and Made Available - Safety Drills Documentation: During the inspection the operation did not have  documentation of fire extinguisher, smoke  detectors, carbon monoxide detectors being  completed on a monthly basis. This was corrected  during the inspection by the checks being  completed and documented.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Records Maintained and Made Available - Safety Drills Documentation (26 TAC §747.801(7))

occurrences.finding: Written Activity Plan - Develop and Follow: During the inspection the operation did not have an  written activity plan/schedule for children in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Activity Plan - Develop and Follow (26 TAC §747.2102(a))
